title: Fix the Unflushed File Write
description: The program should write text to a file and have it be readable immediately afterward.
expectedBehavior: After the program runs, notes.txt should contain the full text 'Meeting at 10am'.
actualProblem: The FileWriter is never closed (or flushed). Writer output is often buffered internally, so without a close() call, some or all of the written text may never actually be flushed to disk, leaving the file empty or incomplete.
explanation: File resources should be closed after use, which flushes any buffered data to disk and releases the underlying file handle. A try-with-resources block guarantees close() is called automatically, even if an exception occurs.
